brief.headline: Push for 8–12% price cut: they keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% peers — room to share

priceAsk.summary: Ask for 8–12% price reduction on rigid plastic packaging
priceAsk.target: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for caps (market typical is ₹0.85–0.95/pc); scale across all items
priceAsk.basis: They keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% for similar firms — nearly double. Market ask shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume. Their profit cushion supports a cut.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹2.15 L cash for us

brief.financialLeverage: Triveni is healthy (6.18 safety score, safe zone) with zero debt and keeps 8.5% profit — well above the 4.8% peers keep. Their cash is stuck for 124 days, longer than peers at 114 days, so cash is a bit tight for them. We're tiny at 0.15% of their ₹179.69 Cr revenue, so alone we have little weight — but bundling volume, a multi-year deal, or credibly showing alternates will give us leverage. Their comfort room on profit and our ability to walk means we can push hard on price and terms.

evidence.point: They keep 8.5% profit, nearly double the 4.8% similar firms keep

Their cash is tied up for 124 days vs 114 days for peers — tighter on cash
Moving to 30-day terms frees ₹2.15 L for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers, pharma — strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd

risks: We're a tiny 0.15% customer (₹26.17 L of ₹179.69 Cr) — on our own we have little pull; bundle more volume or play off alternates to gain weight
One risk flag: EPF payment delays — watch for supply hiccups, but they're financially safe overall (6.18 score, safe zone)
Probe42 score is 4/10 and they return only 6.6% on capital vs 12.6% peers — lower efficiency, but safe and profitable enough to negotiate hard
Moving payment to 30 days tightens their already-stretched 124-day cash cycle — get the cut first, then offer faster pay as a trade
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We've reviewed the market and your margins — you keep 8.5% profit vs 4.8% for similar firms, so there's room to share that with us through an 8–12% price cut and tighter terms.
